newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador to introduce convertibility July 1.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador to introduce convertibility July 1.

text.p: Ecuador plans to introduce a Convertibility Plan pegging the local sucre to the dollar on July 1, a senior Economy Ministry official said Thursday.
Roberto Isaias, head of the ministry's economic team, also forecast the state would receive some $2.0 billion in revenues from the privatization of public companies within the next two years.

"Convertibility has been earmarked for July 1 by the president" of Ecuador, Abdala Bucaram, Isaias told a meeting of the Ecuadoran-German Chamber of Commerce. "It will push down interest rates so that they become equivalent to those in dollars," he said.
Bucaram, who took office last August, plans to spell out his Convertibility Plan next Sunday.

Argentina has had a convertibility plan, pegging the peso at par with the dollar, since April 1991. Bucaram has hired former Argentine Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo, the architect of Argentine convertibility, as an advisor.
The plan has drawn criticism from Ecuadoran businessmen, but Bucaram has countered that his decision was "irreversible."
Isaias said the implementation of the new plan should bring about annual economic growth of 5-7 percent.
Privatization and modernization of state companies are expected to produce some $5.0 billion in revenues. "Money will pour in in the next two years," Isaias said.
Monetary authorities took a first step towards convertibility on Tuesday, when the Central Bank announced it would regulate open market operations.
